summary:
AstroHealth is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew health and mission readiness during long-duration space missions. It brings physical health monitoring, mental wellness tracking, health analytics, and preventive care together in one dashboard.

The platform monitors health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, sleep, hydration, mood, and fatigue. Its personalized anomaly detection system compares readings against individual baselines to identify unusual patterns and generates explainable alerts. AstroHealth also connects health indicators to NASA’s five identified hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile or closed environments. NASA DONKI space-weather data provides additional context about solar activity.

The project addresses the challenge of monitoring astronaut well-being in environments where access to immediate medical support is limited. By combining health insights, preventive recommendations, and crew readiness monitoring, AstroHealth aims to help astronauts and mission teams identify potential concerns earlier and make more informed decisions, supporting safer and healthier space exploration.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

AstroHealth is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and mission-readiness platform designed for long-duration space missions. It brings physical health monitoring, mental wellness, health analytics, and preventive care into a unified dashboard.

The platform tracks indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, temperature, sleep, hydration, mood, and fatigue. Its anomaly detection system compares measurements against individual baselines, identifies unusual patterns, and generates explainable alerts. An interactive human body map connects different body systems with potential health risks. The Five-Hazard Intelligence module organizes health concerns around the five major hazards of spaceflight. The platform also incorporates NASA DONKI space-weather observations to provide context about solar activity.

Additional features include crew health comparisons, preventive health routines, telemetry import through CSV and JSON files, and mission health reports.

What benefits does it have?

  • Provides a centralized view of physical and mental well-being.
  • Helps identify unusual changes in health measurements.
  • Provides understandable alerts instead of simply displaying numbers.
  • Encourages preventive care through personalized recommendations and routines.
  • Helps mission teams compare crew readiness and monitor potential concerns.
  • Provides space-weather context relevant to radiation-related mission risks.

What is the intended impact?

AstroHealth aims to support astronaut well-being and safer long-duration space exploration. It can help astronauts and mission teams recognize potential health concerns, monitor trends, and make more informed decisions, especially when immediate medical assistance from Earth is difficult to access.

What tools and technologies were used?

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
  • Framework: TanStack Start
  • Data visualization: Recharts
  • AI integration: Groq API integration
  • Space-weather data: NASA DONKI API
  • Data processing: PapaParse for CSV imports
  • Storage: Browser localStorage
  • Testing: Vitest
  • Development and deployment: GitHub, VS Code, and Vercel

No dedicated medical hardware or wearable sensors were used. Astronaut health measurements in the demonstration are simulated, while NASA DONKI provides external space-weather observations.

How is the project creative and innovative?

AstroHealth goes beyond a conventional health dashboard by combining personalized anomaly detection, an interactive body map, five-hazard-aware health insights, mental wellness monitoring, and crew-wide readiness in one platform. Its explainable alerts help users understand what changed and why it may deserve attention. It connects individual health indicators with the broader challenges of living and working in space.

What factors did the team consider?

The team considered the unique challenges of spaceflight, including radiation exposure, microgravity, isolation, limited access to medical assistance, and environmental constraints. We also considered the importance of individual health baselines, understandable alerts, data privacy, usability, and preventive care. Medical limitations were taken into account: the platform is intended for monitoring and awareness, not as a substitute for professional medical evaluation or validated diagnostic systems.
